beginner.headline: Wednesday: the long-period south swell starts fading but is still well up regionally, and wind turns light onshore from the south. Evening forecast, so confidence is lower than a same-morning report; your morning on-site check decides.
beginner.recommendation: Plan on 9–11 AM on the rising tide. Watch Canoes from about 8:30 AM for several full set cycles and the post-set current before committing. Wrap up well before evening, when showers and isolated thunderstorms are forecast.

general.headline: South swell peaks tonight and starts fading Wednesday, with light onshore south wind. Early morning at exposed Town breaks is the pick for competent intermediate to advanced surfers.
general.size_note: NWS Oʻahu south-facing shores forecast: 6–8 ft tonight, 5–7 ft Wednesday. Exposed-shore heights, not Canoes.
general.surface: Light texture; light south–southeast wind is onshore on the South Shore
general.waikiki_note: Protected Waikīkī stays much smaller. Longboards and high-volume boards.
general.trend: Fading slowly Wednesday; staying near seasonal norms this week; another long-period swell this weekend, near advisory level

tide.rule: High tide is not automatically the best lesson time. Combine tide with swell, current, wind and the student.

current.during_sets: Stronger push possible, mostly in the morning
current.field_test: Watch how far you and the student are moved by one complete real set, and how much work it takes to get back in position.
current.one_student: Higher tolerance. You can shadow and manage drift.
current.multi_student: Lower tolerance: separation, more retrieval, less control. If current is strong, split the group, take one at a time, or reschedule.
